headline: Jazz snap the Lakers' 9-game winning streak; Luka calls his night 'unacceptable'
detail: Keyonte George scored 30 as Utah won 109–97. Doncic shot 10-of-28 with nine turnovers, and ESPN asks whether his record usage could hurt the Lakers' title hopes.

headline: Anthony Edwards has 'no clue' when he'll be back from knee surgery
detail: The Timberwolves star is upbeat about the long term but has no return date.

headline: Giannis beats his old team as the Heat edge the Bucks 137–130
detail: In his first game against Milwaukee since the trade to Miami, Antetokounmpo and the Heat held on late. Bam Adebayo said he has moved past his issues with Tyler Herro, and the Bucks fell to 1–14.

headline: Lillard says he warned Giannis the grass isn't always greener
detail: Damian Lillard, now in Portland, reflected on advising Antetokounmpo before his move to the Heat.

headline: Nuggets erase a 17-point deficit to beat the Celtics 105–101
detail: Nikola Jokic had 24 points, nine assists and eight rebounds, and Jamal Murray added 21 points and four steals.

headline: 76ers come back on the Magic and stay perfect in clutch games (11–0)
detail: Philadelphia overcame another 17-point deficit, with Embiid, VJ Edgecombe and LeBron James leading a 121–116 win.

headline: Cooper Flagg scores 33; the Warriors are still winless since Curry's injury
detail: Dallas beat Golden State 116–94 to end a three-game skid. P.J. Washington added 21.

headline: Grizzlies set a franchise record with an 8th straight road win
detail: Memphis beat Cleveland 124–121 and is 11–4, fifth in the West.

headline: Rockets beat the Pacers but lose Alperen Sengun to an injury
detail: Kevin Durant scored 21 in a 119–104 win. Watch Sengun's status: Houston is 12–4, third in the West.

headline: Randle calls the Nets' 30-point loss to the Bulls 'embarrassing'
detail: Chicago won 137–107, its easiest win of the season, and Julius Randle publicly questioned Brooklyn's effort and pride.

headline: Kings lose a 7th straight as Booker and Brooks score 29 each
detail: Phoenix won 128–107. Sacramento is 1–13, last in the West.

headline: Wizards snap an eight-game skid behind Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa
detail: Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds; the rookie Dybantsa added 23 and 12 in a 103–99 win over Toronto.

headline: Dylan Harper out 1–3 weeks (hip strain); Julian Champagnie gains
detail: Tests avoided a major injury. Champagnie moves into a bigger role and is a 12-team add for threes and steals.

headline: Don't chase Bucks and Pacers hot nights: their rotations are a mess
detail: Locked On warns that Milwaukee and Indiana minutes swing with absences and odd coaching calls. Herro and Jaquez are down to about 23 minutes lately.

headline: Evan Mobley out 7–10 days (toe sprain)
detail: Cleveland will re-evaluate him around Nov 26–29. Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor get extra minutes meanwhile.

headline: Kawhi Leonard (knee) out at least another week
detail: He has progressed in strength and conditioning but won't return before late November.

headline: Must-roster: Jalen Smith, Ace Bailey, Jeremiah Fears, Moussa Diabate, Wendell Carter Jr.
detail: Locked On says these players have steady roles and are still unowned in too many leagues. Fears gains most while Dejounte Murray is away from the Pelicans.
source: Locked On waiver shows, Nov 15 and 18

headline: Sell high: Anthony Black, Pascal Siakam, Norman Powell, Kevin Huerter, Saddiq Bey
detail: Their numbers are boosted by injuries around them or unusual shooting. Locked On suggests cashing in before they fall back.

headline: Buy low: Brandon Miller, Trae Young, Cameron Boozer, Ivica Zubac, Ajay Mitchell
detail: All are shooting well below their usual levels. Expect a rebound; target them from frustrated managers.

headline: Hot adds Brice Sensabaugh and Quentin Grimes are short-term streams
detail: Both are playing big minutes only because starters are out in Utah and Los Angeles. Expect their roles to shrink.

headline: Dejounte Murray requests a trade
detail: Wait for the actual deal before making big moves; for now, Jeremiah Fears is the clear winner.

headline: Bridges, Josh Hart and Daniel Gafford are losing minutes
detail: Their minutes have dropped without an injury to explain it. Be ready to move on if it continues.

headline: Week 5 schedule: Timberwolves, Trail Blazers and Knicks are the best to stream
detail: Their games fall on lighter days, so their players fit into lineups more easily. Hornets players only play twice.
